commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Ui class for console I/O
commitResults.messageBody:
Move welcome/goodbye, command reading, error display, and task
confirmation messages out of Kiwi into a dedicated Ui class so
user interaction is separated from command handling and task logic.
Behaviour is unchanged; this is the first step toward the Level-9
OOP structure (Ui, Storage, Parser, TaskList).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList to own the in-memory tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Wrap ArrayList operations (add, delete, get, mark, size, index
checks) in TaskList so Kiwi no longer manages the raw list.
Ui now displays via TaskList instead of ArrayList. Persistence and
messages stay in Kiwi so TaskList stays free of I/O concerns.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser to interpret user commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Move command recognition and argument parsing (todo/deadline/event/on
and task numbers) into Parser, which returns a ParsedCommand. Kiwi
only executes: update TaskList, save, and show UI feedback. Index
range checks stay with the list so Parser stays free of TaskList
dependencies.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Wire Kiwi as instances with path-based Storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Refactor Kiwi to match the Level-9 sample shape: constructor takes a
file path, holds Ui/Storage/TaskList as fields, and run() drives the
loop. Storage is now constructed with that path instead of a hardcoded
static file, so save location is injectable while default behaviour
stays ./data/kiwi.txt.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Introduce Command pattern for chatbot actions
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace ParsedCommand plus Kiwi.execute with an abstract Command and
concrete classes (Add, Delete, Mark, Unmark, List, On, Exit). Parser
now returns Command objects; Kiwi.run uses parse → execute → isExit
with try/finally dividers, matching the Level-10 stretch shape.
Ui.showGoodbye prints only the message so the loop owns the lines.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Align Java sources with SE-EDU coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Java sources use mixed import grouping, incomplete Javadoc tags, and
switch-case indentation that do not match the SE-EDU intermediate
standard.

Course work is assessed against that standard. Inconsistent style makes
reviews harder and risks style-guide marks.

Let's bring production and test Java into line with that standard.

The edits are style-only; program behavior is unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add SE-EDU Java coding standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Agents have only generic Javadoc guidance and no project rule that
points to the SE-EDU Java coding standard.

Course Java is judged against that standard. Without a mandatory skill
and agent rule, generated code can drift from it.

Let's add the seedu-java-coding-standard skill and require it in agent
files for all Java work.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Commit messages follow only a brief "include rationale" note. Visual
diffs still point at a missing craft-commit-message skill.

Course Git work is judged against the SE-EDU Git conventions. Agents
need a single mandatory skill so subjects, bodies, and branch names
stay consistent.

Let's add the seedu-git-standard skill and require it for all commits.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody: Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Kiwi uses exceptions for bad user input and save-file problems, but
internal contracts (non-null parsed values, in-range indexes after
validation, recognized save-file types) are not checked at runtime.
A failed assertion means a programmer bug, not a user mistake. Without
these checks, such bugs surface later as NPEs or index errors.
Let's assert those assumptions in Parser, Storage, TaskList, task
classes, and commands. Enable assertions in Gradle test/run and the UI
test runner so they actually run during development.

Each command word is detected with the same equals-or-starts-with
pattern, and arguments are sliced with the same substring-and-trim
logic.

Repeating that pattern for every command makes parse() noisy and
makes a typo in one command word easy to miss.

Let's name the command words and extract isCommand() and argumentOf()
so parse() only maps each command to its handler.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Return each command without nesting
commitResults.messageBody:
parse() chains every command in an else-if ladder, so the unknown-
command case sits in a final else and each successful parse is nested
inside the previous miss.

The happy path for a recognized command should be a straight return,
and the remaining case should clearly mean "everything else".

Let's return as soon as a command matches, and throw for unrecognized
input only after those checks.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Clarify deadline and event field checks
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and event parsing combine separator, description, and date
presence into one compound condition, and the event usage message is
duplicated.

A reader has to decode the nested empties to learn which field is
missing, and the magic " /by " strings hide the command syntax.

Let's name the delimiters, spell each check as a boolean, and share
the event usage text.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Mark, unmark, and delete each copy the same out-of-range check and
the same "no task number N" message, and they all add 1 to turn a
list index into the number shown to the user.

That duplication makes a future wording change easy to apply in only
one of the three commands.

Let's keep the check and the 1-based conversion in Command so each
subclass only describes what it does with a valid index.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Save lines are built and parsed with raw " | ", "0", "1", and field
counts, so a reader must infer what each literal means.

Those same values appear in Task, Deadline, Event, and Storage, which
makes an inconsistent separator easy to introduce.

Let's name the separator, done flags, and field counts, and quote the
separator when splitting so the regex is not a hidden trick.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Parse save lines via TaskType
commitResults.messageBody:
Save-file type letters are compared as raw "T", "D", and "E" even
though TaskType already owns those icons.

Using strings for a small set of known kinds hides that the value is
an enumeration, and it can drift from the icons Task writes.

Let's resolve the icon through TaskType and switch on the enum, with
a default branch for unexpected values.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Split save-line parsing by task type
commitResults.messageBody:
parseLine both validates shared fields and builds a Todo, Deadline, or
Event, so one method mixes several levels of detail.

That mix makes the per-type rules harder to read and pushes the method
well past a comfortable length.

Let's keep parseLine at "split, validate, create, mark done" and move
each type's field rules into its own helper.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Extract unusable-file checks from load
commitResults.messageBody:
load() repeats the same "could not load" prefix and empty-list suffix
for directory, non-file, and unreadable paths.

That repetition buries the successful read path under three similar
guard blocks.

Let's collect those reasons in one helper so load() can return early
and keep reading lines as the main path.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Event: Spell out inclusive date-range checks
commitResults.messageBody:
occursOn() uses two negations in one expression, so a reader has to
invert isBefore and isAfter to see that the range is inclusive.

Let's name each bound check so the inclusive from-to meaning is
obvious.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Kiwi: Rename shadowing isExit in run
commitResults.messageBody:
run() declares a local isExit that hides the instance field used by
the GUI after getResponse().

A reader can mistake the CLI loop flag for the same exit state the
window checks, or assume one assignment updates both.

Let's name the loop flag shouldExit so the two are clearly different.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: Extract numbered listing and task-count text
commitResults.messageBody:
List, find, and on all print "N.task", and add/delete both build the
"Now you have N task(s)" line with the same ternary.

Copying that formatting makes a wording tweak easy to apply in only
one of the call sites.

Let's format numbered rows and the count message in one place each.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Task: Remove comments that restate the code
commitResults.messageBody:
getStatusIcon() and setKiwi() had comments that only repeated what
the code already shows, and the FindCommand constructor Javadoc had
no summary sentence.

Comments should explain purpose to a later reader, not narrate the
next line.

Let's drop the redundant remarks and give FindCommand a header that
says what the constructor is for.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: MainWindow: Use names that explain intent
commitResults.messageBody:
GUI code used k, img, tmp, db, and a bare 1-second delay, so a reader
has to guess what each stands for.

Short names are fine for tiny loop indexes, not for objects that live
across a method.

Let's use kiwi, image, children, and dialogBox, and name the delay
before the window closes.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Name the user-number to index conversion
commitResults.messageBody:
parseTaskNumber() subtracts 1 from the parsed integer in the same
expression, so it is easy to miss that the command uses 1-based
numbers and the list uses 0-based indexes.

Let's parse the number the user typed, then convert it, so those two
steps stay distinct.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

The save-line parser rejects a done flag with a double-negative
compound condition, then computes isDone with a second comparison
against the same literals.

That makes the 0/1 rule harder to read than two named booleans.

Let's name the done and not-done cases and reuse the done flag when
marking the restored task.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams for find and save
commitResults.messageBody:
find() builds a match list with a loop, and save() builds save-file
lines the same way.
Those steps are a filter and a map, so the loop boilerplate hides
the actual transformation.
Let's use streams for those two operations. Other loops stay as
loops because they need indexes or per-line exception handling.
